early-startup-pitch.name: Early-Stage Startup Pitch
early-startup-pitch.summary: Seed and pre-seed pitch arc tuned for vision-heavy stories where revenue and traction are still thin. Anchors the narrative in market change, founder insight, and credible early signal — not metrics yet.

beats.name: Logo
beats.description: Cover slide with the company name, logo, and one-line positioning. Simple, branded, confident.

beats.name: Monumental Change
beats.description: Open by naming a large, undeniable shift in the world. Tech, regulatory, behavioral. The shift is the reason this company exists — investors should feel its weight before they hear about the product.

beats.name: Past Struggle
beats.description: Show what the world tried to do about the problem before the shift, and why those approaches fell short. Honest credit to predecessors makes the new game more credible.

beats.name: Innovative Breakthrough
beats.description: Present the founding insight or breakthrough that makes a new approach possible. This is the 'secret' the company is built on — name it plainly.

beats.name: Unique Offering
beats.description: Detail the product or service. Lead with the customer-visible thing they touch; the architecture can wait. Show why this offering is structurally different from the past struggle.

beats.name: Costly Issues
beats.description: Quantify the pain customers experience without your offering. Time, dollars, opportunity cost. Specific numbers convert sympathy into urgency.

beats.name: Effective Solutions
beats.description: Demonstrate the customer outcome your offering produces. Before/after numbers from early users, even small N. Early-stage pitches are won by leading indicators, not by trailing ones.

beats.name: Unit Economics
beats.description: Explain the financial model. Cost to acquire, gross margin, payback. Investors don't expect maturity — they expect that you've thought about it.

beats.name: Talented Team
beats.description: Introduce the founders and key early hires. Show why this team uniquely sees and can execute on this opportunity. Insight beats résumé at the seed stage.

beats.name: Traction
beats.description: Showcase the early signal: pilots, design partners, waitlist, retention data, anything credible. Frame it honestly — investors at this stage discount inflation aggressively.

beats.name: Investment Opportunity
beats.description: Detail the round size, structure, and use of funds. Tie the raise to specific milestones it takes the company to. Specificity here signals operational maturity.

beats.name: Closing Logo
beats.description: Close on the brand and contact info. Leave the room with the line you most want repeated when the partner pitches you to the rest of the firm.

marketing.name: Marketing
marketing.summary: Marketing professionals analyzing campaign performance, brand metrics, and growth strategies.
marketing.description: Marketing professionals reviewing campaign performance, brand metrics, and growth strategy. Make the funnel visible, highlight engagement metrics, keep the brand consistent, and tell the story visually. Moderate chart density; 15-30 slides.

decide.name: Drive a Decision
decide.summary: Frame options, evidence, tradeoffs, and a recommendation so the audience can choose.
decide.description: Use when the deck exists to get a yes/no, select among options, approve a recommendation, or resolve ambiguity. Lead with the decision needed and make the ask explicit.
decide.outcome: The audience makes or authorizes a clear decision.

formal.name: Formal
formal.summary: Polished, restrained voice for board, investor, and regulator audiences.
formal.description: Authoritative without being cold. Use third-person constructions, full sentences, and concrete numbers. Avoid hedges and humor that depend on shared in-jokes; rely on clarity and precision to land.
voiceCues: Use third person and the corporate 'we' sparingly.
Lead with the recommendation, then evidence.
Quote concrete numbers; avoid round-tripping ranges.
Prefer full sentences to bullet fragments on key claims.
samplePhrases: Q4 revenue grew 18% year over year, led by enterprise expansion.
We recommend approving the Series B raise at $30M.
Net retention was 124%; gross retention was 96%.

classic.name: Classic
classic.description: A timeless, clean, and versatile theme with balanced color contrasts and classic typography. Ideal for professional, readable presentations.

pastel-red.name: Pastel Red
pastel-red.summary: Soft red and blue accents for approachable consumer stories.
pastel-red.description: A pastel red scheme with warm neutrals and blue support, suited to friendly, human-centered decks.

cool-horizon.name: Cool Horizon
cool-horizon.summary: Cool blue-green palette tuned for professional business decks.
cool-horizon.description: A balanced cool-toned scheme with deep navy, business blues, and teal accents. It works well across strategy, finance, and technical narratives.

constantia.name: Constantia
constantia.description: Constantia is a serif OPF font scheme for Latin presentations, using Constantia for both headings and body text.

tenorite.name: Tenorite
tenorite.description: Tenorite is a sans serif OPF font scheme for Latin presentations, using Tenorite Display for headings with Tenorite for body text.

cover.name: Cover
cover.summary: The opening slide: title, subtitle and an optional picture.
cover.description: Open a presentation with its subject and a short introduction. Add a picture when it helps establish the context.

text.name: Text
text.summary: Prose. Several blocks sit side by side when short and stack when long.
text.description: Explain one idea in continuous prose. Use paragraphs or flowing blocks for detail that needs to be read in sequence.

chart.name: Chart
chart.summary: One to six charts, with an optional note.
chart.description: Give a chart enough space to show its evidence. Use the title to state the conclusion and labels to explain the measures.

list.name: List
list.summary: Bulleted or numbered points; one long list flows into columns.
list.description: Present several related points in a clear sequence. Use bullets for independent points or numbered items for an ordered list.
